title: The DOCX paragraph index is built by the first paragraph query, not by every document()
code_state: two files under crates/litchi-docx/src changed; one integration test file extended; no public signature, error type, output byte, limit or unsafe block changed
reason_codes: DocumentPart::from_part and the unmanaged branch of the source-backed Package::document() built a ParagraphIndex on every call, although only paragraph_count, paragraphs, paragraph(i) and the source-backed paragraph_text(i) read it and eight other readers do not

the index was already a best-effort cache whose error is swallowed with .ok(), so deferring the identical expression to the first consumer keeps exactly the same operations able to observe exactly the same swallowed failure
ADR 0005 prescribes lazy loading of semantic payloads into thread-safe caches whose behaviour is semantically invisible; the eager build was the part that did not match

the budget-managed source-backed branch is deliberately left eager because its index carries an execution-budget charge, and moving that charge is a contract change needing its own frozen design record

accepted_evidence.instruction_counts: callgrind isolation pairs on a scratch probe, two document shapes (200 and 10,000 paragraphs), eleven operations, both legs: document() alone -69.30%, document()+text() -34.88%, document()+write_text_to -19.47%, document()+tables() -40.99% on the 10,000-paragraph document; the removed scan is 45.01 M Ir and 70.5% of the text-extraction pass itself; every paragraph query 0.6-0.7% cheaper
accepted_evidence.allocation_counts: the same isolation pairs with a counting global allocator: document() 51 -> 26 allocations and 345,293 -> 2,558 bytes; document()+text() 1,984,218 -> 1,641,483 bytes; paragraph queries identical on both legs
accepted_evidence.native_cycles: perf stat -e cycles isolation pairs, 15 per leg per order, before/after/after/before, medians: document() -68.34% against an A/A floor of -0.01%, document()+text() -39.81% against +1.60%, document()+paragraph_count() -0.69% against -1.67%
accepted_evidence.paired_timing: order A1 B1 B2 A2, 30 samples and 3 warmups per leg, pinned to CPU 12; docx_file_eager_full_text -40.22% and docx_file_source_full_text -32.37% at p50 against A/A floors of 1.52% and 0.66%
accepted_evidence.differential_corpus: 332 documents (62 .docx under test-data/, 270 .docx retained by the change-0483 and change-0495 fuzz campaigns), each signed across ten query families on both the eager and the source-backed facade with every error captured as its Display text; the four signature files are byte-identical between legs
accepted_evidence.tests: five added (three unit, two integration) covering that text, table, element and block reads never fill the cell; that every paragraph query matches the streaming selectors it replaces; concurrent first queries on both facades; and that the budget-managed branch keeps its eager index and its UnsafeEdit refusal
accepted_evidence.gates: cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy -p litchi-docx --all-targets, cargo test -p litchi-docx (1,454 passed, 0 failed, 31 ignored), cargo doc -p litchi-docx --no-deps, tools/non_iwork_gate.py check, tools/check_crate_boundaries.py, tools/check_report_claim_classification.py -- all exit 0

accepted_costs.reported_regression_harness_boundary: docx_semantic_one_paragraph and docx_semantic_list_paragraphs regress by a factor of 2.2e4 and by 1,836% at p50, because the harness builds the document view before starting the clock, so the scan that used to happen in untimed setup now happens inside the timed interval; the same lifecycle costs 0.64-0.68% fewer instructions
accepted_costs.reported_regression_unexplained: docx_file_eager_paragraph_count regresses 5.49% pooled at p50 (both orders agree, +6.07% and +4.90%, A/A floor 0.78%), which is above the 5% review trigger; the same operation pair measured directly is 0.69% cheaper in native cycles and in instructions, and the first measured call after a harness-style untimed preparation takes the same number of page faults on both legs, so the attribution is unresolved and is recorded as an open question
accepted_costs.floor_above_5_percent: the A/A floor exceeded 5% at p50 on docx_file_eager_open_full_text_lifecycle (8.54%), docx_semantic_open (17.34%) and docx_semantic_one_paragraph (69.2%); for those three the counts and not the timings carry the result
accepted_costs.latency_distribution_shift: paragraph readers pay the same scan later; a lazily cached value moves cost from the open into the first query, which is intended and is what ADR 0005 asks for
accepted_costs.clone: a source_backed::Document cloned before its first paragraph query builds its own index, one extra scan per clone
accepted_costs.instruction_counts: instructions rank work, not latency; native cycles were taken beside them for the four headline operations

known_gaps.managed_route: the budget-managed source-backed branch still scans on every document(); deferring it moves an execution-budget charge and needs a frozen design record
known_gaps.corpus: the probe fixture is synthetic and carries no mc: markup, so visible_document_xml takes its cheap presence-scan path and the index's share of document() on a real producer file is unknown
known_gaps.not_measured: cold cache, physical devices, range sources, peak RSS, concurrency scaling, real-producer documents, other platforms
known_gaps.observed_not_acted_on: after this change write_text_to costs 101.9 M Ir and about 90,000 allocations more than text() on the same 10,000-paragraph document; change 0587's DOCX-3 names preflight_semantic_xml as a candidate but the difference also contains the streaming parse and the sink, so no attribution is made

withheld: any registered performance claim, cold-cache, physical-device, range-source, peak-RSS, concurrency-scaling, real-producer or cross-platform result
